clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old male presented with thrombocytopenia. Initial CBC also revealed monocytopenia. Bone marrow biopsy and aspirate showed a normocellular marrow with a B-cell infiltrate (30-40% cellularity) composed of medium-sized mature forms with oval nuclei and cytoplasmic projections. Immunophenotyping of these B-cells demonstrated positivity for CD19, CD20, CD22, HLA-DR, FMC7, kappa monoclonal, partial CD25, CD103, Annexin A1, DBA44, BCL1, BCL2, and TRAP, while being negative for CD5, CD10, LEF1, and BCL6. Molecular testing confirmed the presence of a BRAF V600E mutation. These findings are highly characteristic and diagnostic of Hairy Cell Leukemia.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial CBC showed monocytopenia (absolute monocyte count 0.1596 K/μL).

Bone marrow morphology revealed normocellular marrow with a 30-40% B-cell infiltrate, consisting of medium-sized mature forms with oval-shaped nuclei and appreciable cytoplasm with cytoplasmic projections.
Bone marrow immunophenotyping showed B-cells positive for CD19, CD20, CD22, HLA-DR, FMC7, kappa monoclonal, and partially positive for CD25 and CD103.
Bone marrow immunophenotyping further showed B-cells positive for CD20, Annexin A1, DBA44, BCL1, BCL2, and TRAP, and negative for CD5, CD10, LEF1, or BCL6.
Molecular testing confirmed the presence of a BRAF V600E mutation.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific peripheral blood smear findings for hairy cells were not documented.
Presence or absence of splenomegaly on physical examination was not documented.
